runs.text: Incentives change the expected benefits or costs of a choice, so they can alter behavior at the margin. A congestion fee raises the cost of the next downtown trip. Incentives can be monetary or nonmonetary, and different people may respond differently. A reward can also improve a measured result while harming the underlying goal.

transcript.sourceText: A city adds a $4 congestion fee for a rush-hour trip. Assume other trip costs are already deducted from each driver's benefit. A driver with a remaining benefit of $3 avoids the trip because the fee exceeds that benefit. A commuter with a remaining benefit of $10 still travels. The fee changes choices at the margin without making every driver respond alike.

GENERAL ECONOMICS
GEN-ECON-02
Time: 4 minutes
Outcome: Predict behavioral responses and unintended consequences created by incentives.
Difficulty: Beginner
THE CORE IDEA

Incentives change the expected benefits or costs of a choice, so they can alter behavior at the margin. A congestion fee raises the cost of the next downtown trip. Incentives can be monetary or nonmonetary, and different people may respond differently. A reward can also improve a measured result while harming the underlying goal.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
A speed bonus makes workers finish faster, but quality falls.
A new toll reduces traffic on a busy road.
A toll is added to a crowded bridge, and some drivers switch routes.
A school rewards high test pass rates.
An incentive changes the payoff to a choice; it need not be monetary or guarantee a result.
WATCH OUT

A common mistake is to define incentives as cash payments or guaranteed behavior. An incentive changes the expected payoff to a choice; it may be monetary or nonmonetary, and people can respond differently.
WORKED EXAMPLE: RESPONDING TO INCENTIVES

A city adds a $4 congestion fee for a rush-hour trip. Assume other trip costs are already deducted from each driver's benefit. A driver with a remaining benefit of $3 avoids the trip because the fee exceeds that benefit. A commuter with a remaining benefit of $10 still travels. The fee changes choices at the margin without making every driver respond alike.
